I applied student accommodation but failed to get the offer, so I found it on my own.
Try to get advice from someone you know or your friends might know who reside there. Overall the accommodation market is similar to Danish one.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try to navigate the course website at first and find out if there are courses that are available and you are interested in. Courses at SU are not intense compared with here at KU, so you want to do something you reallly have interests in.
Try socializing more if you live in corridor rooms, and make friends to get through the winter time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It gave me knowledge and academic communication with excellent professors from Anthropology, Sociology and from a big picture, Social Sciences. I really appreciate that part.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Winter in Sweden is even tougher and you would expect even less sunlight, compared to cph.
